key_highlights: Bond market volatility rattles Wall Street and drags ASX lower; ASX finishes flat as miners offset oil-stock weakness
RBA signals further rate hikes as inflation pressures persist, squeezing household spending
AUD sharply weakened against USD amid US economic outperformance
Australian flash PMI sags, signalling softening domestic activity
Trump diesel export ban threat poses significant fuel-cost risk for Australia
Gold miners (Critical Resources, Aurum) surge on new project funding; rare earths (Jupiter) gain on offtake progress
Jetstar industrial action escalates with staff waiving baggage/seat fees
Property market cools as listings rise and demand falls
Energy policy debate intensifies; Labor and Coalition both face credibility challenges
Syngenis gains precision medicine firepower; IDP plummets on China-linked tech controversy

sectors.trend: Miners rose to support ASX flat close; gold names (Critical Resources, Aurum) surged on project funding; Jupiter rare earths advanced on Critica offtake. Oil stocks struggled despite higher crude.
sectors.implications: Gold and rare earths offer relative strength amid rate-hike cycle. BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX benefit from commodity resilience but face headwinds from AUD weakness and global demand softening (PMI sag).

sectors.trend: RBA rate-hike cycle continues, supporting NIMs but pressuring household balance sheets and mortgage demand. Bond market volatility adds uncertainty to yield curves.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from higher rates short-term but face credit-risk and property-exposure concerns as property prices cool. Bond-market stress could compress equity valuations.

sectors.trend: Oil prices jumped on supply concerns; Trump diesel export ban threat creates fuel-cost anxiety. Domestic energy policy debate (nuclear, renewables) unresolved.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WDS.AX face policy uncertainty. Fuel-cost fears (headline 35) could pressure transport and consumer sectors. Nuclear energy debate (headline 31) is a long-term structural theme.

sectors.trend: Syngenis gains precision medicine capability; migrant doctors filling GP gaps highlights structural workforce issues.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX remains defensive anchor. Syngenis (SYG.AX) gains near-term catalyst. Healthcare sector offers relative stability amid rate-hike environment.

sectors.trend: Jetstar industrial action escalates; RBA hikes squeeze household spending; property demand weakens. Fuel costs rising.
sectors.implications: QAN.AX faces operational disruption from Jetstar action. WES.AX, CWP.AX face margin pressure from input costs. Consumer discretionary under pressure.

sectors.trend: $16B Aussie tech firm faces China-link controversy; global tech (AMD $1T, Apple AI chips) shows strength but Australia-specific tech lags.
sectors.implications: IDP.AX plummets on China-linked controversy. Domestic tech remains underweight in ASX. Global AI/semiconductor strength (NVDA, AMD) is a US-market theme, limited ASX spillover.

key_themes: RBA rate-hike cycle vs inflation credibility
AUD/USD weakness driven by US outperformance
Bond market volatility as cross-asset risk
Trump trade/diesel policy as external shock vector
Gold and rare earths as inflation/rate hedges
Property market cooling and housing affordability
Migration policy reform and labour-market implications
China exposure as corporate and geopolitical risk

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA further rate hikes and household spending compression
risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight financials (NIM benefit) and quality dividend payers; underweight rate-sensitive REITs and consumer discretionary

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Trump diesel export ban / fuel supply disruption
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor energy stocks (WES.AX, WDS.AX); hedge transport exposure; watch fuel price indices

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Bond market volatility spilling into equities
risk_assessment.mitigation: Maintain liquidity; avoid over-leveraged positions; use bond yields as timing signal for equity entries
Favour export-oriented miners (BHP.AX, RIO.AX) that benefit from weaker AUD; avoid import-heavy consumer names

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Jetstar industrial action and transport disruption
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce QAN.AX exposure short-term; monitor union negotiations for resolution timeline

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Property market deterioration and credit risk
risk_assessment.mitigation: Underweight REITs and property-linked financials; monitor NAB.AX/CBA.AX mortgage book quality

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold miners on rate-hike and geopolitical uncertainty
opportunities.rationale: Critical Resources and Aurum show first-mover advantage; gold benefits from inflation, AUD weakness, and bond-market stress

opportunities.recommendation: Position in rare earths / critical minerals on offtake progress
opportunities.rationale: Jupiter Rare Metals gaining Critica offtake traction; structural demand from EV/defence supply chains

opportunities.recommendation: Selective financials overweight for NIM expansion
opportunities.rationale: RBA hikes support net interest margins; banks remain high-dividend defensive plays amid equity volatility
Syngenis precision medicine catalyst; CSL provides portfolio stability in rate-hike environment

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce exposure to oil/energy stocks amid policy uncertainty
defensive_moves.rationale: Oil stocks struggling despite higher crude; domestic energy policy gridlock creates binary risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim QAN.AX / Jetstar exposure pending industrial resolution
defensive_moves.rationale: Escalating union action with fee waivers signals operational and revenue disruption
Rising listings, falling demand, and rate hikes create downward pressure on property valuations

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge AUD weakness with export-oriented miners
defensive_moves.rationale: AUD pulverised by US boom; BHP/RIO revenue in USD benefits from weaker dollar

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain range-bound to slightly lower. Bond-market volatility, RBA hike expectations, and PMI softness cap upside. Miners and gold provide support; oil, consumer, and REITs drag. Jetstar action and fuel-cost fears add near-term noise. Key watch: upcoming jobs data and RBA commentary.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook cautiously constructive if RBA peaks and inflation moderates. Gold, rare earths, and healthcare offer structural growth. Property correction may create selective REIT entry points by late 2026. Trump trade policy and diesel ban remain wildcard risks. Migration reform could support labour supply and wage moderation.
